A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiffDecompose and contain complete, readable main text and appendices. Their equations, three tables, fifteen figures, and inference algorithm support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AlphaBlend and LOGO experiments, component ablations, foreground-reconstruction results, and a 30-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, foreground-reconstruction results, and user study.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendices B–C retain the same In-Context Decomposition, Layer Position Encoding Cloning, multimodal attention, training loss, and inference algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six AlphaBlend subtasks and LOGO-H, LOGO-L, and LOGO-G. No evaluated dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Inpaint Anything, SDXL-inpainting, Flux-ControlNet, PowerPaint (labelled PowerPoint in tables), and ClipAway. The reference revisions introduce no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training budgets, image resolutions, dataset sizes, mask dilation, and RMSE/SSIM/LPIPS/FID evaluation remain unchanged. Appendix D.4 retains the same 30-participant study and randomized presentation of six methods.

E4.justification: The LPEC ablations in Table 2 and Figure 6, ICD ablation in Figure 7, SDXL strength sweep in Figure 9, and failure examples in Figure 15 are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The user-study reporting remains aggregate votes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the user-study charts in Figure 13 match, as do qualitative examples and reported findings. For example, Table 1 retains LOGO-H RMSE 3.2321 and LOGO-L FID 24.20 for DiffDecompose.

T1.justification: The compositing definitions, posterior formulations, positional-encoding relations, attention equation, and appendix loss and inference formulas are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the transparent/semi-transparent decomposition task, AlphaBlend dataset, and DiffDecompose with ICD and LPEC. Novelty and effectiveness claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations of inpainting-baseline failures and the LOGO-L FID disadvantage. Appendix E preserves the pixel-drift limitation, proposed future guidance masks, and broader-impact discussion.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including Flux.1 initialization, LoRA rank 128, batch size 1, learning rate, H20 hardware, and appendix training/inference details. Code and dataset release remain promised upon acceptance, with the same repository address.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including MotionBooth, SemFlow, and work on in-context segmentation and 3D point-cloud understanding, while removing previously uncited bibliography entries. The related-work narrative and positioning against existing decomposition methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammar and wording corrections in the abstract, introduction, and related work, and updates affiliations and correspondence markers. The section organization and narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained with layout adjustments: Figure 3 moves above Section 3.3, and Figure 4 moves from page 8 to page 7. Appendix text is enlarged, and Table 3 shares page 20 with discussion instead of occupying an otherwise nearly empty page.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves readability through copyediting, larger appendix text, and closer placement of results with their discussion. It also resolves an unresolved Section 2 citation and refreshes the references. These are limited editorial gains; the scientific evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
